input.prompt: Inspect the project to locate the game code and determine why steering controls are inverted. Identify relevant files and control mapping. Do not edit; report concise findings.

content.text:
<subagent sessionID="ses_e522ac8ccffehSD5Ymp66SuM6j" state="completed">
- **Input mapping:** [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/input.js`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/input.js#L156) maps **A/← to negative X** and **D/→ to positive X**. The touch joystick uses the same horizontal direction.
- **Driving:** [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game.js`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game.js#L616) uses `mv.x` as steering. Positive steering increases the car’s heading; the resulting forward vector turns toward +X, i.e. right when facing +Z.
- **Vehicle orientation:** [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/models.js`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/models.js#L64) places the front lights at +Z, matching the driving direction convention.

I don’t see an inverted left/right mapping for forward driving in these files. One notable behavior is that heading change is multiplied by `Math.sign(car.speed || 1)` ([`game.js:635`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game.js#L635)), so steering feels reversed while reversing—consistent with the car’s rearward motion.
</subagent>
